entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom 15.59.0
entries.content:
### Added

- **layout: an auto-hiding bar drawn outside its body (`useAutoHideBar`, `AutoHideBarBody`, `AutoHideBarRegion`, `AutoHideBarBand`).** The hook holds one region's state and motion; the body slides the content it wraps; the region draws the band, controls and summary strip wherever its owner places it. One window toolbar shared across tabs follows the current tab's controller, so switching tabs never mounts a toolbar per tab. `AutoHideBar` is now the hook, a body and a region in one box (unchanged).
- **app-shell: translucent drop zones (`panelLayout.drop.appearance: 'translucent'`).** A translucent pane over the page (white at 0.45, a 0.08 edge, a 0.1 dash in the foreground's ink, the accent at 0.12 when active), a desktop browser's split targets; `surface` stays the default.
- **app-shell: a hidden retained panel painted behind (`hiddenPresentation: 'behind'`).** Still inert and out of the accessibility tree, under the shown panels, for content that shows itself during a gesture (the page a profile swipe brings in).

### Consumers

Bump to 15.59.0. Opt-in.

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom 15.58.0
entries.content:
### Added

- **app-shell: retained panels (`panelLayout.retain`, panel `stack`).** Every panel's content stays mounted as a child of one region in the order its id was first seen; reordering panels, moving one into or out of a `stack` and hiding or showing it change only its box. Nothing remounts, no DOM node moves (an iframe is never taken out of the document, so its page never reloads) and a hidden panel keeps the region's full size, invisible and inert rather than `display: none`, so it shows again without a relayout. Boxes are fractions of the region plus fixed offsets, the same on the web and native, so a resizing region moves them with no JavaScript. Dividers commit proportional `spans` within `minWidth`/`minHeight`; drop zones and `resizeHandle` work as on any split. A desktop browser's tabs as split panes. Gates: an iframe sentinel (no iframe added to or removed from the document across rotate, stack, hide and return; fails when the region follows the panels' order), native mount counts, geometry and divider tests; the **Retained Panels** story.

### Consumers

Bump to 15.58.0. Opt-in.

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom 15.57.0
entries.content:
### Added

- **app-shell: `useAppShell()`'s `navigationDock.moving` / `topBarDock.moving`.** True from a hide or show until its motion lands, so an app can lay its pages out once when the region's room has settled instead of on every frame of the slide.
- **app-shell: a peek's own backing and per-edge inset (`peek.chrome`, `peek.inset` as `{ top, bottom, start, end }`).** `chrome` gives the `surface` backing its `surface`, `border`, `borderWidth` and `shadow` for a region whose palette is not the theme's (a window tinted by its profile); a desktop browser's top-strip peek sits 4 from the top and 6 from the sides. The dock types (`AppShellDock`, `AppShellDockPeek`, `AppShellDockPeekChrome`, `AppShellDockMotion`, `AppShellDockState`, `AppShellEdges`) are exported.

### Changed

- **app-shell: a `manual` peek is its host's to close.** With `peek.trigger: 'manual'` the floating region no longer closes when the pointer leaves it; the host that opened it (a native window edge watcher with its own hold region, the panel plus some slack) calls `peek(false)`. `hover` is unchanged.

### Fixed

- **app-shell: the peek's shadow is no longer cut at its edge.** The floating region clipped itself, backing and all; the content now clips inside it and the backing's shadow falls around the region.
- **app-shell: a navigation with an explicit `variant` renders once on the web.** The CSS compositor mounted the navigation's content twice (a panel and a rail copy, one hidden by CSS) even when the rail could never show; a navigation whose variant never changes (no `navExpandedFrom` tier) now mounts only its own mode, halving its render work and its subscriptions.

### Consumers

Bump to 15.57.0. Everything is opt-in except the two fixes and the `manual` peek's close, whose only consumer (Astro) drives it from its edge watcher.

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom 15.56.1
entries.content:
### Fixed

- **surface presence: content that changes while a surface fades no longer turns a material inside it flat.** `useSurfacePresenceContent` fades each piece of a surface's content that holds no material host. When content changed during a fade, React could reuse a faded piece's node for new content that did hold one. The piece kept its fading `opacity` and `filter` and became a backdrop root over the new host. A hover card whose profile finished loading as it closed, for example, drew its Follow button without blur for the rest of the close. In Chromium this failed on 5 of 10 close timings from 40 to 150 ms before the load, and on 5 of 5 runs of `verify-backdrop-root.mjs` on that story. Each change is now reconciled before the frame paints. A piece that has come to hold a host is handed back at once, and its own pieces take the presence instead. Class changes count, and content that changes while the presence is still rising to 1 is covered too. Pieces already headed for the presence finish their fade instead of jumping to its end.

### Consumers

Bump to 15.56.1. No API change.

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom 15.56.0
entries.content:
### Added

- **app-shell: a peek that fades as it slides (`peek.fade`, `motion.peekFadeIn` / `peekFadeOut`).** A docked sidebar or top bar's peek fades in as it slides in and out as it slides out, on the slide's own motion unless given its own `MotionSpec` (a desktop browser's default peek: 180 ms, ease-out cubic, fading with the slide). Hiding, showing and docking from a peek keep the region whole. It never fades a material host or its ancestors: on the web the fade is a registered progress on the host (`--bloom-nav-peek-fade`, `--bloom-top-peek-fade`) that the material inside reads as its `--bloom-surface-presence`, while the backing and the content fade piece by piece over the same curve; in Chromium the fade, a row and a material button's layer stay on the curve frame for frame with no material ancestor faded (`scripts/verify-peek-fade-and-pill.mjs`). Native fades the host from a shared value. Reduced motion lands it at once.
- **layout: `ResizeHandle variant="pill"` and `thickness`; app-shell: `panelLayout.resizeHandle`.** A split's divider: a 4×36 bar, radius 2, centred on the separator in the foreground colour, invisible at rest, 32% under the pointer or keyboard focus and 55% while dragging, on a strip the gap plus 2 px of each pane (11 for a 7 px gap). Same drag, keys and semantics as the grip; logical insets for RTL; hover and drag held in state on native, including react-native-macos's mouse events. Astro drew its split dividers by hand.

### Fixed

- **layout: reduced motion now stops the resize handle's fade.** The reduced-motion rule was less specific than the rule that sets the 150 ms fade, so the grip still faded.

### Consumers

Bump to 15.56.0. Both additions are opt-in; the dock host's content gains one wrapper view, laid out as before.

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom 15.55.0
entries.content:
### Added

- **app-shell: a navigation and a top bar that leave the layout and peek back (`sidebar.dock`, `topBarDock`).** Hidden, the region gives its whole room to the content and its content stays mounted, inert and out of the accessibility tree; resting the pointer on its edge floats the same tree 5 from the window's edges over a content that does not move, and docking from the peek lands in place. The slot and the content's offset are two readings of one progress (a registered CSS custom property on the web, a shared value on native), so the content's edge follows the navigation exactly: within 0.1 pt of the spring in Chromium. Motion is data: hide and show default to a desktop browser's measured sidebar spring (response 0.215 s, ratio 0.79), the peek to 0.185 s / 0.77 in and 150 ms out. `useAppShell()` gains `navigationDock` and `topBarDock` (`hidden`, `setHidden`, `toggleHidden`, `peeking`, `peek()`, native `progress` values). Astro's window drew all of this by hand.
- **app-shell: `frameInset` and `background="transparent"`.** The framed region's distance from each window edge (top 6, end 7, bottom 7 for a desktop browser's card) without changing the gutter between panels; and a shell that paints nothing, so a window's own material shows between its regions.
- **app-shell: proportional splits (`panelLayout.spans` / `onSpansChange`).** Resizing between two flexible panes commits their weights instead of freezing pixels, so a split keeps its proportion as the window resizes. `AppShellPanels` takes them too.
- **app-shell: panel drop zones (`panelLayout.drop`).** Edge targets on each panel for a drag the app owns (a tab dragged out of a strip), staged as measured (rest, grown, active, leaning 43% toward the pointer), hit by the dragged picture's overlap with hysteresis, logical in RTL, localized, painted from tokens. `resolvePanelDropTarget` and `panelDropZoneRect` are exported.
- **layout: `AutoHideBar`.** A toolbar that steps aside to a strip with a summary (a page's host) when its owner says so, peeks back over the body on hover (150 ms in, 250 ms out) and returns on press; the body is laid out once per change and slid, never re-laid every frame.
- **motion: springs and timings as data.** `MotionSpec` (`{ response, dampingRatio }` or `{ duration, easing }`), `animateWithSpec` for Reanimated, `motionCss` for a CSS transition (a spring as a sampled `linear()` curve), and the closed form (`springProgressAt`, `springSettleMs`, `motionProgressAt`) for tests that compare motion with recordings.

### Changed

- **app-shell: flexible split panes resolve from a zero basis on native, as the CSS compositor always did.** Native used to start them at their minimum and share the rest: 1:2 spans with 100 minimums in 800 were 300/500 on native and 267/533 on the web; both are now 267/533.
- **app-shell: a content-aligned shell with `contentMaxWidth="none"` no longer centres its envelope in CSS.** The envelope fills the row; native already aligned it to the frame's start.

### Consumers

Bump to 15.55.0. Every addition is opt-in; shells that set none of the new props render as before, except the two changes above.

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom 15.54.0
entries.content:
### Added

- **agent-chat: `AgentChatHistory` can be a chat panel's history.** `framed={false}` (what the workspace already used inside) is public: the rail fills its container and paints nothing. `query` / `onQueryChange` draw the conversation-list search pill, filtering nothing themselves; a thread's `group` captions contiguous runs ("Today", "Previous 7 Days") in place of "Recent"; `onEndReached` (once per approach, `onEndReachedThreshold` 200) and `after` page a long history. Astro's chat sidebar drew all of this by hand beside a rail that could not.
- **questionnaire: `detail` on a question and `footer={false}`.** `detail` draws what the question is about between the prompt and the answers; `footer={false}` drops the step pills and Previous / Next for one `single` question that a pick answers. Together they make an agent's tool approval (Allow, Always Allow in This Chat, Don't Allow, over the tabs it would open) the same docked question card as any other, where Astro had drawn its own.

### Consumers

Bump to 15.54.0. Defaults are unchanged.

entries.title: @alia.onl/sdk 22.4.0
entries.content:
- **A shared conversation shows its artifacts.** `readSharedConversation` keeps an assistant
  message's `artifacts` (`AliaSharedArtifact`: `{ id, type, title, data }`, the canvas tool's
  result) and `sharedMessages` hands each to the thread as the canvas call that drew it.
  `AliaSharedConversation` draws them inline under their reply on the canvas renderers (reports,
  decks, dashboards, charts, tables). An `AliaThread` that is not `readOnly` is unchanged: in the
  app an artifact still opens in the canvas panel, not in the reply.
- The server sends `artifacts` only from the API that ships with this release
  (`docs/agent-embedding.md` §6); against an older API the shared page shows words and images,
  as before.

entries.title: @alia.onl/sdk 22.3.0
entries.content:
- **Decks and dashboards on the canvas.** `CanvasComponent` draws the canvas tool's two new
  types: a `deck` (one card per slide: title, subtitle, bullets, body) and a `dashboard` (its
  stats in a row, then charts, tables and notes on the chart, table and Markdown renderers).

entries.title: @alia.onl/sdk 22.2.0
entries.content:
- **Awaited host tools.** `AliaHostToolDefinition.awaitsResult: true` declares a tool whose
  result the model reads in the same turn ("this tab's text"). When the model calls it, the
  runtime runs the host's `execute` once and POSTs `{ toolCallId, outcome, detail?, result? }` at
  once to `/v1/chat/turns/:turnId/host-results` through the authenticated API (with the app
  assertion), instead of queueing the outcome for the next request. `AliaHostOutcome.result`
  carries a string or JSON value of at most `HOST_RESULT_MAX_CHARS` (100,000) characters as JSON;
  a larger one is answered as `failed`. A failed POST is reported to `AliaHostTools.onUndelivered`
  and never retried. `parseHostAction` keeps `awaitsResult` and `turnId`.
- **Personalization off for one turn.** `AliaTurnRequest.personalization: false` (read at send
  time from `host.turnRequest()`) sends `personalization: false`: Alia reads no memory and offers
  no memory tools for that turn. Nothing is sent otherwise.
- `awaitsResult` is sent only for a tool that declares it, so existing hosts send the same bytes.
  A host that declares one needs the Alia API receiver for awaited host tools deployed first
  (`docs/agent-embedding.md` §2); an older API refuses the field with `invalid_host`.

entries.title: @alia.onl/sdk 22.1.2
entries.content:
- **Every entry type-checks under `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`.** The SDK ships source, so a
  consumer compiling with `"noUncheckedIndexedAccess": true` (Astro) type-checked the SDK under
  it too and got errors from indexed reads in the runtime, thread, citation and catalogue-tool
  modules (27 from `@alia.onl/sdk/runtime` alone). Each read is now narrowed where the index is
  known to be in range, with a loop over the values where that is simpler. Behaviour is unchanged.
- `check:entry-types` compiles every entry with `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` on, so CI keeps it so.

entries.title: @alia-codea/cli 3.1.0
entries.content:
Ctrl+C requests authenticated Stop for the current generation and waits for its
acknowledgement before closing the stream. Every tool continuation has its own
turn ID; Stop blocks further tools, including approvals resolved late. Incidental
teardown and broken output pipes only detach. Account changes fence both lanes. Acknowledged Stop retains visible partial text
without incomplete tool calls; account teardown never saves that partial reply.

Uses the shared server SDK 1.3.1 wire parser and removes the unused OpenAI dependency.
Requires Node 22 or newer, matching the shared SDK and current CLI dependencies.

entries.title: @alia.onl/server 1.3.1
entries.content:
Preserve streamed `delta.tool_calls` as typed `tool_calls` events, including
fragmented arguments and indices, so terminal consumers can share the wire reader
without losing client-owned tools. Invalid tool fragment shapes fail explicitly.

entries.title: @alia.onl/sdk 22.1.1
entries.content:
- A delayed Stop acknowledgement cannot idle a newer turn, replace its sidebar
  preview, or notify a different conversation. Thread/account changes and unmounts
  invalidate old completion callbacks while the original acknowledgement drains.
- Keep repeated Stop requests deduplicated during that drain; errors from an old
  Stop cannot appear in a replacement thread. Public APIs and peer ranges are unchanged.

entries.title: @alia.onl/server 1.3.0
entries.content:
- Add optional typed `turnId` to chat requests and `cancelTurn()` for explicit
  authenticated Stop. Aborting a stream remains transport detachment.
- Add `createAliaTurnControl()` for early IDs, deduplicated Stop acknowledgement
  and transport cleanup; callers retain their shared account fencing.
- The explicit Stop receiver must be deployed first. Supported control lanes are
  human sessions and exact app-only credentials; delegated services without a
  verified original actor retain their existing chat behavior without `turnId`.

entries.title: @alia.onl/sdk 22.1.0
entries.content:
- Stop explicitly cancels the authenticated foreground turn across API replicas;
  closing a sheet or losing its transport still allows background completion.
- Export `createChatTurnControl` / `AliaChatTurnControl` from `@alia.onl/sdk/runtime`
  for custom Stop controls, with account-change fences and early-turn ids.
- Requires the explicit Stop API receiver to be deployed before adoption; see
  `docs/explicit-chat-stop.md` in the repository.

entries.title: @oxy.so/core 7.5.0
entries.content:
### Added

- `OxyInferenceClient.getGenerationRecordByIdempotencyKey(key, options)` reads
  authoritative settled usage after a response was lost before its request id.
  It uses the existing credential-bound API, preserves delegated attribution,
  and supports financial receipts and internal metered records. Missing or
  pending records remain errors, never zero-cost results or inference retries.

entries.title: @oxy.so/core 7.4.0
entries.content:
### Changed

- Complete the finite own-workload protocol transition: `serviceToken()` and
  `serviceTokenFor()` now request scope-free protocol 2, as shared service clients
  already do. All workload token paths share the recipient cache and invalidate
  it after a 401. Deploy only after old producers are stopped or migrated and
  their bounded tokens have drained.
- Retire the verified legacy-workload introspection projection in service
  middleware. Current own callers still require live workload, environment,
  recipient and requester checks. Explicit customer credentials, external service
  tokens, OAuth/MCP scopes and public SDK signatures retain their contracts.

entries.title: @alia.onl/sdk 22.0.1
entries.content:
Remove the Bloom peer upper bound to follow the first-party package policy.
The required minimum remains `15.10.1`; core `>=7.1.0 <8` and services
`>=13.0.0 <14` are unchanged. This patch changes package metadata only.

entries.title: @alia-codea/cli 3.0.2
@alia.onl/sdk 22.0.0
entries.content:
Requires `@oxy.so/core >=7.1.0 <8` and `@oxy.so/services >=13.0.0 <14`.
Text, dictation, speech and voice use the shared account transport. Account
switches and sign-out invalidate pending work; websocket credentials are
refreshed through the shared origin-bound getter before connecting. Own Oxy
apps use their current account without app scopes or consent. External
credentials retain their existing limits.

entries.title: @alia.onl/server 1.2.0
entries.content:
Adds `createAliaForOxyService` and `createAliaTransportForOxyService` for
Oxy workload transport with Alia’s canonical audience and verified requester
context. The `./internal` entry shares the authenticated API/gateway protocol
without importing React or a server SDK through the client entry. Existing
external credential clients remain supported.

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom 15.51.0
entries.content:
### Added

- **item: `titleNumberOfLines` and `subtitleNumberOfLines`.** Where a string title (default 1) and subtitle (default 2) truncate; `0` never does, the same contract as `GroupedSectionItem`'s `titleNumberOfLines` and `descriptionLines`. An explanatory row had no way to show its sentence whole: Commons' "how it works" rows ended mid-sentence ("incluso cuando ...", Pixel 8a, Spanish).

### Consumers

Bump to 15.51.0. Defaults are unchanged.

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom 15.50.7
entries.content:
### Fixed

- **page-header, page-footer (`EdgeScrim`): the floating header's fade no longer ends in a hard line on Android.** `react-native-svg` laid the ramp out about 1.55 times taller than its box there, so the box cut it off with half the page colour still showing: a line across the content at the header's foot whenever the page was scrolled (Commons, Allo; Pixel 8a, measured pixel by pixel). Android now draws the ramp as the view's own `experimental_backgroundImage` gradient, which spans exactly its box; other platforms keep the SVG. `edgeScrimGradient(color, edge)` is the gradient string.
- **page-header: a bar with nothing in it is not drawn.** A header with no title, subtitle, back, leading slot or actions (Commons' ID tab, which only owns the status bar) is the safe area and its scrim. Once the bar's minimum height applied on native, that empty bar reserved a 56dp blank band above the content.

### Consumers

Bump to 15.50.7. No API change.

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom 15.50.6
entries.content:
### Fixed

- **Scrollers (`ScrollArea`, `ScreenScrollView`): a control inside takes its tap while the keyboard is open.** React Native's default `keyboardShouldPersistTaps` (`never`) lets every ancestor scroller spend the first tap on dismissing the keyboard, and a tap any one of them swallows never reaches the control. Allo's composer sits inside three of Bloom's (panel, pager, page): with the keyboard up, Send only closed the keyboard and the message stayed in the field (Pixel 8a). Both default to `handled`, which still dismisses on a tap no control takes; a caller's own value wins.

### Consumers

Bump to 15.50.6. A screen that relied on the first tap in a scroller ONLY closing the keyboard (and not pressing what it landed on) should pass `keyboardShouldPersistTaps="never"`.

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom 15.50.5
entries.content:
### Fixed

- **Native sheets (dropdown, context menu, popover, select, hover card, menubar): a controlled one hears every user dismissal.** `useSheetOpenBridge` closed from state a sheet the user had already dismissed (the `open=false` the dismissal itself caused), which fires no `onDismiss`, so its "closed from state" flag stayed set and swallowed the NEXT user dismissal: `onOpenChange(false)` never came, the consumer stayed `open`, and its next open was a no-op. In Allo, after two backdrop taps, holding a message opened nothing until a restart. Only a presented sheet is closed from state now.
- **chat-composer `ReactionPicker`: emojis are whole on native.** The cell's `padding: 0` shorthand lost to Button's `paddingHorizontal: 8` (React Native ranks a longhand above the shorthand whatever the order), leaving a 14dp slot in a 30dp cell; every emoji in the message menu's reaction bar was cut in half. The cell passes longhands, as does the voice recorder's "slide to cancel".

- **message-bubble: "This message was deleted" is legible on your own bubbles.** It was drawn in the theme's `muted`, which knows nothing about the fill behind it, and on the outgoing accent bubble it was dark on dark. It now takes the side's meta ink (AA against that fill). Italic lines (the deleted line, "Forwarded from") keep 2dp after the text, because Android measures advances, not ink, and clipped the slant of the last letter.

### Consumers

Bump to 15.50.5. No API change.

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom 15.50.4
entries.content:
### Fixed

- **message-bubble: swipe-to-reply no longer swallows every touch.** `activeOffsetX` is the range the finger may travel WITHOUT activating (RNGH activates when `dx < start` or `dx > end`). `SwipeToReply` passed `[-9999, -12]` (incoming) and `[12, 9999]` (outgoing), ranges that exclude 0, so the pan activated on the first move event and cancelled the JS responder. On Android (Allo, Pixel 8a, with 15.50.3) holding a message still opened no menu. It now activates only past 12 towards the centre: `[-9999, 12]` and `[-12, 9999]`.
- **chat-composer `AttachmentMenu`: every disc in a row is top-aligned.** Button hands `alignItems` to its content, a row, so the cell's `'center'` centred each disc vertically and those beside a wrapped caption ("Photos and videos") sat lower. The cell now passes `'flex-start'`.
- **message-media `PollMessage`: no gap under the question after a vote.** Once results show, the "Select one" hint goes, but its `Text` stayed, empty, and took a line on Android. The subline is drawn only when it has something to say.
- **zoomable-media-gallery: the overlay viewer dims to nearly opaque on Android.** It renders in the app's own window, where Android draws no blur (and a blur target crashes), so its backdrop was expo-blur's fallback tint plus the 0.28 dim and the conversation stayed readable behind the photo. On Android the overlay now drops the blur layer and dims to 0.92; other platforms keep the shared blur.
- **app-shell: the overlay navigation drawer clears the status bar.** The drawer is portaled to the app root, full screen, but cleared the device insets only when the shell owned the safe area (`safeArea`). In an app whose Screens own their insets (Allo) it ran under the status bar, the clock over its logo. It now always pads `12 + insets`.
- **Menus (dropdown, context, select rows): the icon no longer touches its label on native.** The row's gap lived only in `rowClass` and never reached the row on Android ("QSearch"). It is inline as well (`columnGap`, the size's `gap`), unless a caller `className` restyles the row.

### Consumers

Bump to 15.50.4. No API change.

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom 15.50.3
entries.content:
### Fixed

- **chat-list: a swipeable row no longer looks selected on a phone.** The row's swipe face is opaque so the panes cannot read through it, and it was painted `theme.colors.background`, the page. On a phone the list sits in a `card` panel, so in Allo's light "Raspberry" theme every row was a #ffe8ed slab on a #fff8f8 panel, the look of a selected conversation. Every chat-list part now resolves its paint off `useSurfaceFill()`, the colour the enclosing surface actually painted (as `mail-list` already did): `resolveChatListPaint(theme, surface)`, whose second argument defaults to the page. Hover, selected and placeholder fills step off that surface too. `SwipeRow` without a `background` defaults to the ambient surface instead of the page.
- **message-bubble: holding a message opens its menu on native.** On Android holding a message opened nothing. The body text was `selectable` on every platform and a selectable text view takes the long press for its own selection; it is now selectable on web only (native copies from the menu). The `media` slot's pressables (picture frame, file row, contact and place cards, poll rows, voice note controls), deeper than the bubble, took the touch with no long press; they now hand on the bubble's `onLongPress` through an internal context (`message-media/context.ts`). `PlayButton` takes an optional `onLongPress`.
- **zoomable-media-gallery: the overlay's share button is visible in a light theme.** It was the light `surface` material with a hard-coded white glyph, a blank disc over the viewer in Allo's light theme. The overlay's share button and web arrows are now the same scrim chrome as the counter pill (`rgba(0,0,0,0.55)`, white), since the dim under them is dark in every theme. `appearance="page"` keeps its own palette.

### Consumers

Bump to 15.50.3. Additive API only (`PlayButton.onLongPress`). Outside a surface that publishes its fill, row colours do not change.

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom 15.50.2
entries.content:
### Fixed

- **chat-composer `AttachmentMenu`: every item is reachable on Android.** The grid was one wrapping row of Buttons, and Android's Yoga gave its first line the whole sheet (176dp) and its second 8dp, so in Allo's six-item menu Contact and Poll were clipped out of a sheet that had already sized itself for them. The grid is now explicit rows of `columns` cells; a short last row keeps the columns. A caption takes two centred lines instead of an ellipsis ("Photos and …").
- **chat-composer `ComposerAttachmentStrip`: a picture's tile no longer prints its file name.** The line under a tile is the upload's progress, the caller's `caption`, or, for a glyph tile only, the name. A photo staged in Allo read "100.png", the name Android's picker gave it. The name stays the tile's accessible name and the remove button's.

### Consumers

Bump to 15.50.2. No API change.

entries.title: @oxy.so/app-preset 5.2.0
entries.content:
### Security

- Ships the Oxy Updates code-signing certificate,
  `certs/oxy-updates-code-signing.pem` (RSA 2048, CN=Oxy Updates Code Signing,
  SHA-256 `E9:1D:40:E6:…:39:DA:81`, valid to 2036-10-24). Every OTA-enabled
  binary built with this preset verifies manifest signatures.
- `withOxyUpdates` now FAILS CLOSED, as its README already said: the default
  `codeSigning` is `'require'` (it was `'auto'`, which only warned and produced
  a binary that accepts unsigned manifests for its whole lifetime). A
  certificate file that is not a PEM certificate, or an unknown `codeSigning`
  value, is refused. `'auto'` and `false` remain for local development builds,
  explicitly.

entries.title: @oxy.so/app-preset 5.1.0
entries.content:
### Fixed

- Metro answers an OPTIONAL require (`try { require('x') }`, an `import()` in a
  `try`) that lands on a native package Expo autolinking does not link with
  "not found", which is what the probe sees on a clean install. Commons 1.3.0
  crashed on launch from a checkout whose bun store kept a stale hoisted
  `node_modules/.bun/node_modules/@expo/ui` (57.0.17, in no lockfile):
  expo-router's `@expo/ui/jetpack-compose` probe found it and SDK 57 JS ran
  against an SDK 58 binary that never linked it. Static imports are unchanged
  (warned about once). `metro/linked-native-packages.js`.
- A RELEASE bundle (Metro `dev: false`, or NODE_ENV=production) refuses a
  workspace package's `dist/` that was not built from the checkout's `src/`.
  The same 1.3.0 build bundled a five-day-old `packages/contracts/dist` (Zod 3
  era) whose module scope called `innerType()` against Zod 4, and a core from
  before the commit's own KeyManager changes. A package opts in with
  `"oxySourceStamp": "dist"` and runs `metro/source-stamp.js` last in its
  build (core, contracts, protocol, telemetry and expo-splash do); the check is
  by content, so a checkout round trip that only changes mtimes passes. A
  package that does not opt in is only warned about, by mtime.
  `metro/fresh-workspace-builds.js`.

entries.title: @oxy.so/services 13.6.0
entries.content:
### Fixed

- The account members screen reads member handles with `users.lookupMany` and fails the query when a chunk failed, so React Query retries it. With `getMany` a failed read resolved empty and members showed their raw id for the whole five-minute stale window. Requires `@oxy.so/core` ^7.3.0.

entries.title: @oxy.so/core 7.3.0
entries.content:
### Added

- `users.lookupMany(ids): Promise<BatchLookup<User>>` reports every id as `found` (the users), `missing` (its chunk was answered without it: the server says the account does not exist or is not visible — the only list safe to cache as absent) or `failed` (its chunk failed: unknown, ask again), plus `error`, the first chunk failure. It never rejects for a chunk failure. `users.getMany` is now `lookupMany(ids).found`, unchanged in behaviour, and its JSDoc says it conflates failure with absence. Measured in Allo: one `/users/by-ids` chunk failing on a phone left a conversation with no name and a placeholder avatar for five minutes, because the people layer cached every id `getMany` did not return as unresolvable.
- `OxyServer.assets.lookupBySha256(sha256s, { ownerUserId? })` gives the reverse content-address lookup the same three outcomes; `metadataBySha256` is its `found`, unchanged.
- `BatchLookup<T>` is exported from the root entry.
- `KeyManager.getRecoveryMnemonicForCurrentIdentity()` returns the stored phrase only when it derives the key on this device, and `null` otherwise. It throws `IdentityUnavailableError` when storage cannot be read, like `getRecoveryMnemonic`.

### Fixed

- An aborted request is classified by whether the SDK's own controller fired, not by the error's name. Expo's `fetch` (the global `fetch` of Expo 52+ native apps) rejects an abort with a plain `Error` — `fetch failed: Fetch request has been canceled` — so on a phone the 5 s per-attempt timeout surfaced as `NETWORK_ERROR` with `status: 0`, and a caller's cancellation as a network failure the retry loop tried again. A timeout is now `TIMEOUT` (`timeout: true`, `Request timed out after <n>ms`) and a cancellation `CANCELLED` on every platform. A GET that times out is therefore no longer retried on React Native, matching the web (`retryOnTimeout` opts in).
- `identity.rotateKey` stores the new recovery phrase once the new key is persisted on the device. The phrase slot used to keep the replaced key's phrase, so Settings revealed a phrase that recovers nothing and the device backup lost its phrase. If the new phrase cannot be stored, the replaced one is deleted.
- `deleteIdentity` retries a failed device-backup clear once, then overwrites the record with a tombstone that restores nothing. A failed clear used to leave the full key in a store (Android Block Store) that is restored silently on the next launch without keys, so a deleted identity could come back.

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom 15.50.1
entries.content:
### Fixed

- **select: the trigger's inner padding is back on Android.** The field's geometry (row, border, gap, padding longhands, min height per size) was only ever in classes, and in 15.50.0 Allo's "Raspberry + Antique Gold + Cobalt" sat flush against both ends of the pill. It is now inline as well on both forks, unless a caller `className` restyles the field; `fieldStyle` still overrides it. Shrink-to-line and truncation from 15.50.0 are unchanged.

### Consumers

Bump to 15.50.1. The chevron is `<SelectIcon />` inside `SelectTrigger`; a trigger that does not render one draws none (Allo's Appearance → Colour trigger has only `<SelectValue />`).

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom 15.50.0
entries.content:
Six defects measured on Allo's Android release (Bloom 15.48.0, React Native 0.88 Fabric, Pixel 10 Pro / Pixel 8a).

### Fixed

- **portal (native): content keeps the React context of where `<Portal>` is written.** The native portal is a context + outlet, because `ReactFabric.createPortal` can only replace a whole root's children. The outlet re-rendered the stored element and re-published only Bloom's theme, so any provider between the app-root outlet and the portal was lost. Allo's Settings → Account crashed with `AlloSettingsProvider is missing`, while web (`createPortal`) worked. The portal now collects every context provider above it from its own fiber, subscribes to each, and the outlet renders the content inside the same providers. React Native's host-position contexts (text ancestor, ScrollView and VirtualizedList), the safe-area insets and frame, the portal's own contexts and Bloom's blur-window contexts are deliberately not carried. An update keeps the portal's place at the outlet, and it re-registers in a layout effect, so it lands in the same frame.
- **settings-modal: an open, idle modal no longer renders every frame.** The saved toast, which stays mounted at opacity 0 while the modal is open, centred itself with `marginLeft: -width / 2` taken from its own `onLayout`. Yoga's pixel rounding flipped that width by one device pixel back and forth forever: 601 frames in 5 s at about 146 % CPU, and uiautomator never went idle. A full-width row now centres it. A new gate replays Fabric's pixel grid and checks, over the modal and every `Dialog` placement, that no host's own `onLayout` moves or resizes that host.
- **settings-modal `SettingsRow`: a wide trailing control no longer crushes the label.** The row wraps in every layout, and the label column is `flexBasis: 0` plus grow plus `minWidth: 140`. The old `flexBasis: 140` never reached Yoga's wrap decision, because Yoga zeroes the computed basis of a row's only grow-and-shrink child. Allo's "Colour" chooser had squeezed the description to about 48dp, one word per line.
- **select: the trigger shrinks to its line and the value truncates before the chevron**, on both platforms (`flexShrink`, `maxWidth: '100%'`, inline value shrink).
- **chat-list `StoriesRow`: two separate strings for your own entry.** The avatar is drawn from `own.name` / `own.avatar` (the placeholder without them), and the caption is always `labels.own`. With no name, the avatar no longer shows the label's first letter ("Y"). Captions use the entry's whole slot (ring plus gap), and your own may wrap to two lines instead of showing "Your sta…". **Behaviour change:** an app that passed `own.name` now sees the label as the caption, not the name.
- **chat-list / mail-list rows: the pressed fill on native comes from Pressable's own `pressed` state.** It used to be a copy kept from press-in/press-out, and Android can drop the press-out when a tap opens a screen, so rows came back still painted pressed. Fixed for `ChatListItem`, `ArchivedRow`, the `ChatSearchResults` rows, `MailRow` and their icon buttons.
- **chat-people `ContactList`: sticky section headings are off by default on Android**, where rows rendered unpainted until the first scroll; `stickyHeaders` opts back in. The cause is suspected, not yet confirmed on a device: the layered (`zIndex`) sticky-heading wrappers between rows.

### Added

- `excludeFromPortalBridge(context)` (`@oxy.so/bloom/portal`): marks a host-position context so native portals leave it at the outlet's value. It returns the context.
- `ContactList layout="flat"` with `flatLabel`, for search results: one section, in the given order, with no A–Z rail and no sticky heading.

### Consumers

Bump to 15.50.0. No code change is needed. Allo can delete its sticky-heading workaround for search lists (use `layout="flat"`) and pass the account's display name and avatar to `StoriesRow`'s `own`.

entries.title: create-oxy-app 0.9.0
entries.content:
### Changed

- The generated frontend declares every required native peer of
  `@oxy.so/services`: `expo-crypto`, `expo-secure-store`, `expo-file-system`,
  `@expo/app-integrity` and `@react-native-community/netinfo` join the ones it
  already listed. Expo's autolinking skips optional peers and an undeclared
  native module installs at whatever version the package manager picks; an app
  without `expo-crypto` built and then had no CSPRNG and no sign-in.

entries.title: @oxy.so/services 13.5.0
entries.content:
### Changed

- **`expo-crypto`, `expo-secure-store` and `react-native-keyboard-controller`
  are REQUIRED peers.** Every app must list them itself:
  `npx expo install expo-crypto expo-secure-store react-native-keyboard-controller`.
  Expo SDK 58's autolinking links the app's dependencies and the NON-optional
  peers of what it walks, and skips optional peers. `expo-crypto` was only an
  optional peer of `@oxy.so/core` / `@oxy.so/protocol`, so in an app that did not
  list it the native module was never linked: measured on a Pixel 10 Pro, Allo's
  Android release failed to start its client with `[oxy.protocol.crypto]
  'expo-crypto' is not installed, so the React Native CSPRNG
  (crypto.getRandomValues) is unavailable … Cannot find native module
  'ExpoCrypto'`, and "Sign in with Oxy" failed at once in
  `generateChallenge()`. `expo-secure-store` (the device credential and the
  shared iOS device session; without it the credential falls back to
  plaintext AsyncStorage) was not declared at all, and
  `react-native-keyboard-controller` was optional although the native
  `KeyboardBoundary` imports it statically. Core and protocol keep them
  optional: they also run in Node, servers and browsers.
- `expo-secure-store` is loaded by a literal `import()` in a `try` instead of a
  runtime-computed specifier. Behaviour is unchanged: Babel evaluates the old
  constant, so Metro resolved the package all along; only this package's own
  gates could not see it.

### Added

- `__tests__/packaging/requiredNativePeers.test.ts` reads every runtime load in
  services', core's and protocol's source and fails on a native module that is
  neither a required peer of services nor recorded as a graceful optional one
  (haptics, pickers, clipboard, push, the third-party OAuth browser, video).

entries.title: @oxy.so/app-preset 5.0.0
entries.content:
### Breaking

- `plugin/withOxyAndroidRelease` is removed; listing it throws with the fix.
  Release signing moved to `@oxy.so/services/plugins/withOxySharedPermissions`
  (services 13.4.0), which every Oxy Android app applies, directly or through
  this preset, and it now FAILS CLOSED: a release build is always signed by
  `signingConfigs.release` from the `OXY_UPLOAD_*` Gradle properties (new:
  `OXY_UPLOAD_STORE_PASSWORD_FILE` / `OXY_UPLOAD_KEY_PASSWORD_FILE`, and the key
  password defaults to the store's), and `oxyVerifyReleaseSigning` fails every
  release variant whose certificate is not the ecosystem one. A debug-signed
  Mention release, built without the properties, had taken ownership of
  `so.oxy.permission.IDENTITY` / `DEVICE_SESSION` on a phone, and every correctly
  signed Oxy app then failed with `INSTALL_FAILED_DUPLICATE_PERMISSION`. Debug
  builds are unchanged unless `OXY_UPLOAD_SIGN_DEBUG=true` opts them in. Delete
  the entry (and any app-local signing plugin).
- The `@oxy.so/services` peer floor is `>=13.4.0`, and the preset refuses an
  older Services: it would declare the permissions without release signing.

### Changed

- `['@oxy.so/app-preset', {}]` applies the R8 `-optimize` ProGuard swap that
  `withOxyAndroidRelease` did (a no-op on Expo SDK 58, whose template already
  uses it).

entries.title: @oxy.so/services 13.4.0
entries.content:
### Changed

- `plugins/withOxySharedPermissions` now also applies the new
  `plugins/withOxyReleaseSigning`: an app cannot declare the Oxy signature
  permissions without its Android release being signed with, and checked
  against, the ONE ecosystem certificate (SHA-256
  `b8ab3746466ce4569d7a6a0ffa1eed91bc375174d503613987ca09cb33d6a58d`, alias
  `oxy`). It replaces `@oxy.so/app-preset/plugin/withOxyAndroidRelease`
  (removed in app-preset 5.0.0) and app-local copies such as Mention's
  `plugins/withAndroidReleaseBuild.js`; prebuild refuses a `build.gradle` one of
  them already edited. Measured on a phone: a debug-signed Mention release took
  ownership of `so.oxy.permission.IDENTITY` / `DEVICE_SESSION`, and every
  correctly signed Oxy app then failed with `INSTALL_FAILED_DUPLICATE_PERMISSION`.
  - The `release` buildType is always signed by `signingConfigs.release`, never
    the debug key. The keystore comes from the Gradle properties
    `OXY_UPLOAD_STORE_FILE`, `OXY_UPLOAD_STORE_PASSWORD` or (new)
    `OXY_UPLOAD_STORE_PASSWORD_FILE`, `OXY_UPLOAD_KEY_ALIAS`, and optionally
    `OXY_UPLOAD_KEY_PASSWORD` / `OXY_UPLOAD_KEY_PASSWORD_FILE` (default: the
    store password). `~/` is expanded.
  - **A release build without the ecosystem key FAILS.** `oxyVerifyReleaseSigning`
    runs before every release variant (`pre…ReleaseBuild`,
    `validateSigning…Release`), opens the release buildType's effective signing
    config and compares the key's certificate with the ecosystem one, so it also
    refuses an EAS-managed or per-app key and a wrong alias. The error says how
    to provide the key and never prints a password. Debug builds never run it,
    and there is no opt-out for release.
  - Opt-in `OXY_UPLOAD_SIGN_DEBUG=true` signs the debug buildType with the same
    key and puts it under the same check (a dev client that can be installed
    next to real Oxy apps). It replaces Willo's `withOxyDebugSigning`
    (`OXY_DEBUG_*`), which prebuild now refuses.
  - An app that declares no Oxy permission (Authenticator) lists
    `plugins/withOxyReleaseSigning` directly.

entries.title: @oxy.so/app-preset 4.1.0
entries.content:
### Fixed

- `import … from 'react-native'` on native no longer loses every name
  NativeWind's `react-native-css/components` shim does not list. React Native
  0.88 added `AssetRegistry`, which Expo SDK 58's `expo-asset` imports from
  `'react-native'`; the shim lacked it, every `useFonts` failed with
  `Cannot read property 'getAssetByID' of undefined`, and Android release builds
  stayed on a blank screen. Metro now resolves that import to
  `metro/react-native.js`: the shim's own getters unchanged, plus a forwarding
  getter for each remaining name of React Native's index. No `node_modules`
  patch is needed (upstream: nativewind/react-native-css#506, #504).

### Added

- `withCompleteReactNative(config, projectRoot)` from `@oxy.so/app-preset/metro`,
  the same fix for an app that still composes `withNativeWind` itself. Apply it
  last.

entries.title: @oxy.so/services 13.3.0
entries.content:
Needs `@oxy.so/core` 7.2.0.

### Added

- `useAccountTheme({ canUse })` applies the account theme to Bloom: the account
  colour always (through `useAccountColor`), the account's mode
  (`user.themePreference.mode`) while this device's theme source is `account`.
  The source (`'app' | 'account'`, default `account`) is a local, per-device
  choice, read synchronously on web so the first paint knows it.
- `useAccountThemeControls()` returns `{ source, changeThemeSource,
  changeThemeMode }` for a settings screen: a mode change applies at once and,
  on the `account` source, is written to the account's portable theme; turning
  the source to `account` seeds an account that has no theme yet. Without a
  session that can reach the account the effective source is `app`.

### Changed

- `useFileDownloadUrl` answers a URL core already resolved in its first render
  (`assets.cachedUrl`), with no request and no loading frame, and returns an
  absolute `http(s)` reference unchanged. A result is never shown for another
  file, variant, expiry or viewer.

entries.title: @oxy.so/core 7.2.0
entries.content:
### Added

- `assets.cachedUrl(fileId, variant?, expiresIn?)` answers, synchronously and without a request, the URL `assets.url` already resolved for the current caller while it is cached. It reads the same identity-scoped cache and TTL as `url`, so another account's scoped media URL is never returned and a trashed, restored, deleted or re-scoped asset is a miss.
- `assets.renderUrl(ref, variant?)` is the URL a render path shows without waiting: an absolute `http(s)` reference unchanged, else the cached resolution, else `publicUrl`. Apps no longer keep their own file-id → URL cache next to the SDK's.
- `HttpService.peekCachedGet(url, params?)` reads the identity-scoped response cache without a request.

entries.title: @oxy.so/services 13.2.0
entries.content:
### Added

- A single query can be kept across restarts for the signed-in account with
  `meta: { persist: 'account' }` (type `AccountQueryMeta`), without declaring
  its root in `accountQueries`: it is written to that account's blob, restored
  before the account cache is ready, dropped from memory on an account switch
  and deleted on sign-out, exactly like a declared root. Meant for the few
  reads that shape a returning user's first paint (tab layout, theme), not for
  lists. Apps that pass no `accountQueries` get this too.

### Changed

- A cold boot that paints a saved session resolves `isAuthResolved` only once
  the account's cached queries are restored (one local read), so the first
  paint already has them instead of shifting a moment later.
- The SDK's query persisters serialize only when a query they keep (or a
  mutation) changes; activity in other queries (feeds, search) no longer
  re-serializes them.
- An account cache whose stored blob cannot be read becomes ready empty
  instead of never becoming ready.

entries.title: @oxy.so/services 13.1.0
entries.content:
### Added

- Runs on React Native 0.81 to 0.88 and Expo SDK 54 to 58 (it needed 0.85 and
  SDK 56). The peer floors are now the Expo SDK 54 stack: `react-native`
  `>=0.81.0`, `expo` `>=54.0.0`, each `expo-*` module at its SDK 54 version,
  `react-native-reanimated` `>=4.1.0`, `react-native-gesture-handler`
  `>=2.28.0`, `react-native-safe-area-context` `>=5.6.0`, `react-native-svg`
  `>=15.12.1`, `react-native-keyboard-controller` `>=1.18.5` and
  `@expo/app-integrity` `>=0.1.10`. `compat/expo-54` installs that stack as an
  external consumer in CI and typechecks, renders and bundles `OxyProvider`
  against it.
- Runs on react-native-macos (Astro). Importing the SDK there used to throw,
  because expo-image and react-native-keyboard-controller have no macOS
  implementation and throw on import. `.macos` forks now draw images and read
  their size through react-native's `Image` and skip the keyboard provider;
  the SDK's own iOS/Android native modules, and the Expo modules macOS lacks,
  are optional at runtime and their features stay off.

### Fixed

- The native OAuth return no longer calls `URLSearchParams.keys()`, which React
  Native's own `URLSearchParams` typings before 0.85 do not declare.

entries.title: @oxy.so/app-preset 4.0.0
entries.content:
### Breaking

- The Babel config no longer adds `babel-plugin-module-resolver`. `@/` resolves
  from the app's `tsconfig.json` paths instead (`"@/*": ["./*"]`), which Metro
  reads by default. An app that imports `@/…` without that path breaks, and its
  Jest config needs `"^@/(.*)$": "<rootDir>/$1"` in `moduleNameMapper`.

### Changed

- In development the Babel config is exactly `babel-preset-expo`. Expo SDK 58's
  oxc transformer, Noxcturnal, runs only when the Babel config resolves to the
  bare Expo preset, and any extra plugin or option sends every file back to Babel.
  The explicit `react-native-worklets/plugin` and `unstable_transformImportMeta`
  are gone because `babel-preset-expo` 58 does both itself. The build-id inliner
  now runs in production only; development already used a constant id.
- The config plugin turns on `experiments.noxcturnalTransformWorker` in
  development (`NODE_ENV !== 'production'`). Production builds stay on Babel:
  Noxcturnal keeps the requires of dead platform branches, which pulled
  `@livekit/react-native` into Mention's web bundle (+6.8% JS). Pass
  `noxcturnal: false` to opt out; an app that sets the experiment keeps its value.
  Measured in Mention with `noxcturnal` 0.1.9: cold Android dev bundle 55.5 s →
  26.0 s, and web 92.9 s → 56.2 s. `noxcturnal` 0.1.5 (`@expo/metro-config`
  58.0.15) fails on TS generic arrows in `.ts` files, so take `expo` 58.0.19 or
  later.

entries.title: @oxy.so/core 7.1.0
entries.content:
### Added

- Service transports expose `fetchReplayable(url, { bodyFactory, ...init })` for streaming uploads. The factory opens a fresh body after authentication, and reopens it only once after a 401 and successful credential refresh. Network errors, redirects, rate limits and server errors never trigger an upload replay. The transport preserves fixed requester identity, origin validation, cancellation and zero-cookie behavior without buffering the upload.

- Linked clients expose `getAccessToken(target, { signal })` for product socket protocols. The shared session handles refresh, destination validation, cancellation and account-change fencing before returning the credential.
- `assets.withMcpDocumentRequester` supports the existing external Homiio document tools through a separate, bounded document proof. Private uploads retain the original external account and live grant, enforce the document size/type limits, and recheck upload provenance on multipart completion.

entries.title: @oxy.so/ship 1.1.1
entries.content:
### Changed

- Package against core 7 and contracts 6. Ship APIs are unchanged.

entries.title: @oxy.so/services 13.0.0
entries.content:
### Breaking

- Own application sign-in and account use no longer expose internal app scope or consent controls. External OAuth connections retain consent and scoped access.
- Require core 7 and contracts 6 for the shared authority contract.

entries.title: @oxy.so/mcp 1.4.0
entries.content:
### Added

- Inject the shared authenticated Oxy transport for catalogue registration, introspection, connections and audit requests. Authentication and refresh stay with core; explicit external credential callbacks remain supported.

### Fixed

- Reject redirects and omit ambient cookies on authority calls.

### Changed

- Require patched Zod 4.6.7 for collection validation.
- Package against contracts 6.

entries.title: @oxy.so/stickers 0.2.2
entries.content:
### Changed

- Package against contracts 6. Sticker APIs and exported types are unchanged.

entries.title: @oxy.so/core 7.0.0
entries.content:
### Breaking

- Server schema validation uses patched Zod 4 and contracts 6; client entry points remain Zod-free.
- Own service authority is explicit and scope-free. Workload callers use shared service transports; external credential pairs retain scoped authority.
- Own workload mint requests reject scope options. Reader-first deployment temporarily preserves v1 only for public manual token calls; internal SDK calls use v2.

### Added

- `createLinkedClient().fetchOptional` keeps the same origin and session fencing while allowing public endpoints to receive anonymous requests when no session exists. Strict `fetch` still requires a session.

- Shared linked-client fetch, recipient-bound service clients, resource introspection for services, keys and sessions, and fixed requester proof clients for Files and other platform calls.
- Optional server-only temporary IAM credential provider and workload-only ecosystem activity publishing.
- Service transports expose destination-checked credentials for product SDK WebSocket protocols, sharing the HTTP transport's workload identity, cancellation and recipient cache. Kaana-only fixed account attribution remains separate from requester data authority.
- Revocable requester context for multiple own-service hops and a separate external MCP media proof, preserving each original account and external grant.

### Fixed

- Prevent redirects, ambient cookies and shared response caches from leaking requester or operation authority across accounts.
- Apply caller cancellation during workload preparation and bound the shared identity exchange, so an unavailable issuer cannot leave product requests waiting indefinitely.

entries.title: @oxy.so/federation 2.12.0
entries.content:
### Changed

- Accept core 7 and contracts 6 alongside the existing compatible runtime versions. Federation exports and wire formats are unchanged.

entries.title: @oxy.so/protocol 1.5.1
entries.content:
### Changed

- Remove the unused Zod dependency; protocol validation continues through the shared client checks.
- Package against contracts 6. Protocol exports and signed wire formats are unchanged.

entries.title: @oxy.so/contracts 6.0.0
entries.content:
### Breaking

- Root schemas and public schema types use patched Zod 4.6.7. Client checks remain Zod-free and match its validation and error codes. Explicit contract checks preserve existing UTF-16 limits, minute timestamps, URL values and integer bounds; oversized bounded collections fail before element validation.
- Distinguish first-party authority without scopes from external scoped service, inference and agent authority.

### Added

- Typed resource introspection preserves service, API-key and human-session identity, original requester, effective account and live account permissions.
- First-party task and operation context contracts preserve requester provenance without storing user bearer tokens.

entries.title: @oxy.so/services 12.14.0
entries.content:
Needs `@oxy.so/core` 6.16.0.

### Changed

- A returning signed-in user's cold boot paints at once: with a session saved
  on the device, the provider shows the account from its cached profile (and
  the account's cached queries), plants a still-valid persisted token and
  resolves `isAuthResolved` before any network. The app's classification and
  the session are then checked in the background: a fresh registry lookup and
  a mint with the app's own device credential, whose commit refreshes the
  profile. If the registry now classifies the app OAuth-only, or the server
  ends the session (`invalid_device_secret` / `no_active_session` with no
  recovery lane restoring one), it signs out at that moment. If neither can be
  asked (offline, a timeout, a 5xx), the cached session stays on screen and is
  asked again on the lost-token backoff and on reconnect. The provider keeps
  the registry's last verdict per clientId and the last profile it held, in
  its own storage next to the account query cache; a sign-out deletes the
  profile, and a profile only paints for the account the saved session belongs
  to.
- A first boot (nothing cached), an identity-bound provider
  (`sessionMode: 'identity'`) and an OAuth return on the URL boot as before:
  the classification and the session hand-off stay on the critical path, with
  their deadlines.

entries.title: @oxy.so/core 6.17.0
entries.content:
### Added

- `ServiceAssetMetadata.hlsRejectedReadyAt` identifies an incorrectly framed
  legacy HLS generation when the original is known H.264 MP4 with AAC
  audio. Consumers can clear an observed readiness stamp no newer than the
  rejected generation, guarded against concurrent replacement, and select the
  original without confusing a missing lookup with an authoritative rejection.

entries.title: @oxy.so/services 12.13.0
entries.content:
Needs `@oxy.so/contracts` 5.8.0.

### Changed

- `useSupervision()` reads the session's supervision state from the cache
  instead of blocking every mount on a fresh request. `OxyProvider` keeps it
  current: fetched when the session is established, refetched when the app
  returns to the foreground and when the session socket signals
  `supervision_changed`. `data` is undefined only while the session's first
  fetch is pending, while the query is disabled and after a failed fetch. The
  return shape is unchanged; the server still enforces supervision on every
  content request.

entries.title: @oxy.so/core 6.15.2
entries.content:
### Changed

- Depends on `@oxy.so/contracts` 5.8.0. No code change.

entries.title: @oxy.so/contracts 5.8.0
entries.content:

entries.title: @oxy.so/core 6.15.1
entries.content:
### Fixed

- `oxyTrustProxy` no longer throws when the client has already disconnected.
  proxy-addr hands it `req.socket.remoteAddress`, which is `undefined` on a
  closed socket, and `req.ip` threw `TypeError: rawIp.trim` from every
  middleware that read it (the rate limiters among them). An address-less hop
  is now never trusted, so `req.ip` is `undefined`, as `resolveClientIp`
  answers for a closed socket.

entries.title: @oxy.so/federation 2.11.0
entries.content:
A remote actor that rotated its key is believed again on its next signed
request, instead of being refused until its stored actor happened to refresh.

### Changed

- `verifyHttpSignature` asks `fetchPublicKey` once more, with
  `{ refresh: true }`, when the key it was given does not verify, and verifies
  against the key that comes back when it differs. An actor that rotates its key
  keeps its keyId, so a stored copy cannot tell the old key from the new one.
- `FetchPublicKey` takes an optional second argument, `FetchPublicKeyOptions`
  (`{ refresh?: boolean }`, exported). An adapter that ignores it still
  satisfies the type, and keeps the old behaviour.
- `ActorResolver.fetchPublicKey(keyId, { refresh: true })` fetches the owning
  actor again and stores what it publishes, unless that actor was fetched in the
  last minute (the key that failed is then the one it publishes, and anyone can
  send a bad signature naming a real keyId). Concurrent refreshes of one actor
  share a single fetch. It resolves the actor from the stored row's URI when
  there is one, rather than the keyId with its fragment cut.
- `createActorRouter`'s `inbound.fetchPublicKey` is a `FetchPublicKey`, and the
  inbox passes the refresh request through to it. An app that wraps the resolver
  passes the second argument on.

entries.title: @oxy.so/app-preset 3.6.0
entries.content:
### Added

- Opt-in `staticHydrationBoundary` Metro adapter for Expo Router 58 static
  exports. The app and document render at separate React roots, matching the
  browser's `#root` hydration boundary and preserving `useId` and workspace DOM.
  Fonts, styles, metadata, loader data and scripts retain their Expo contracts;
  live streaming delegates to Expo unchanged. Version guard and real hydration
  tests protect the private renderer integration.

entries.title: @oxy.so/federation 2.10.0
entries.content:
The identity bridge's transport is typed as core's `serviceRequest`, so an app
passes it straight through and the compiler checks what the bridge names.

### Changed

- `ServiceRequest` resolves to `ResponsePayload<T>` (`@oxy.so/core` 6.14.0):
  `T` is the `{ data }`-unwrapped payload, and a `T` naming the envelope
  resolves to `never`, so reading `.data` off it fails to compile. An app passes
  `serviceRequest` through as is —
  `(method, path, body) => oxy.serviceRequest(method, path, body)`; an adapter
  returning a bare `Promise<T>` still satisfies it.
- Requires `@oxy.so/core` ^6.14.0 (was any major from 1 to 6).

entries.title: @oxy.so/federation 2.9.0
entries.content:
A community's outbox and followers parse on Lemmy and PieFed.

### Added

- `isGroupActorKind(kind)`: whether a local account is announced as a `Group`.
  The moderators route and the Group collection shapes below all ask it.
- `groupOutboxCollection({ id, totalItems, orderedItems })` and
  `GROUP_OUTBOX_SIZE` (50): a `Group`'s outbox as one unpaged
  `OrderedCollection` of its latest `Announce`s, which is what Lemmy's
  `GroupOutbox` requires. A paged outbox with only `first` failed to parse, so
  a Lemmy server that discovered a community backfilled none of its posts.
- `groupFollowersCollection({ id, totalItems })`.

### Changed

- `createActorRouter`: a `Group`'s followers are a `Collection` with
  `totalItems` and `items: []`, the shape Lemmy's `GroupFollowers` reads, on
  every request (including `?page=true`). The follower list is no longer
  served for a community. Other actors are unchanged.
- The `Group` actor carries `sensitive: false`, Lemmy's community NSFW flag.

entries.title: @oxy.so/core 6.14.0
entries.content:
Every SDK read that typed the `{ data }` envelope and read `.data` again came
back empty: the transport had already reduced the envelope to its payload. A
community's moderators, the viewer's follow graph and the store were affected.

### Fixed

- `users.moderators()` answers the community's moderators (it answered `[]`).
- `follows.viewerGraph()` answers the signed-in viewer's following, mutual,
  blocked and restricted ids (each was `[]`); `follows.mutualIds()` and
  `follows.followsOfFollowsIds()` answer their ids (they answered `[]`).
- `store.categories()` answers the shelves (it answered `[]`), `store.app()`
  the listing and `store.reviews.write()` the saved review (both answered
  `undefined`), and `store.reviews.mine()` the caller's review (it answered
  `null`, or threw when they had none).

### Added

- `ResponsePayload<T>`: what `oxy.request<T>()` (and `serviceRequest`, the
  `HttpService` methods and the namespaces' context) now resolves to. `T` is the
  payload the transport delivers; typing the `{ data }` envelope instead
  resolves to `never`, so reading `.data` off it is a compile error. A page
  (`data` beside `pagination` or `nextCursor`) is typed whole, as it travels.
  Every other `T` is unchanged, and a generic wrapper returning `Promise<T>`
  still compiles.

entries.title: @oxy.so/services 12.11.0
entries.content:
Needs `@oxy.so/core` 6.13.0.

### Added

- `AccountSettings` from `@oxy.so/services/screens`: the body of the
  `AccountSettings` surface, for an app that embeds a managed account's
  settings in its own page. `extraSections` renders the app's own sections
  before the danger zone; `onUpdated(account, { cleared })` follows every
  accepted profile write, after the SDK's user cache already holds it, for the
  app's own copies of the identity; `archive` replaces the danger-zone row's
  words (a row with its own `title` shows only its own `description`) and the
  confirmation (a rejection is reported and nothing is archived), runs
  `beforeArchive` after the confirmation and before Oxy's archive (a rejection
  stops the archive), and `onArchived` in place of closing. Without `navigate`, Members opens as a sheet.
- The account settings edit the account's picture — through the same
  source list, cropper and upload as the personal profile — and its
  categories (primary first, "Make primary", the selectable vocabulary to add
  from, at most `MAX_ACCOUNT_CATEGORIES`). A category id this build cannot name
  keeps its row and survives a save.
- `ChangeAvatar` takes an optional `subject` (`{ avatar, displayName }`) to
  preview and offer removing a picture that is not the signed-in user's.

### Changed

- The account settings' Save is enabled only when something changed.

entries.title: @oxy.so/federation 2.8.0
entries.content:
A deleted local actor tells the fediverse once, then answers `410 Gone`.

### Added

- `DeliveryService.federateActorDelete(actorOxyUserId, username)`: the actor's
  `Delete` of itself (`<actor>#delete`, to `as:Public`, the shape Mastodon
  sends), one per follower (shared) inbox, signed with its own key. No consent
  or profile read, since the account is already gone at Oxy. Throws when it
  cannot queue, so the caller retries.
- `createActorRouter({ isActorGone })` and `createWebfingerRouter({ isActorGone })`:
  a username that resolves to nobody and is a deleted actor answers `410 Gone`
  instead of 404: the actor GET with a `Tombstone`, its inbox, its
  followers/following/moderators collections, and WebFinger. That is what
  Mastodon (WebFinger), Lemmy, PieFed and Mbin (refetch) read as permanent.
  Omitted, every miss is a 404 as before.
- `buildActorDeleteActivity(actorUri)` and `goneTombstone(id)`, exported from
  `@oxy.so/federation/node` for the app's own content routes.

entries.title: @oxy.so/core 6.12.0
entries.content:
A file whose bytes are gone for good is `lost` (ADR 0043 D13): kept, so its
owner and the applications using it see why it no longer opens, and never
served.

### Added

- `AssetStatus` (`AssetLiveStatus | 'lost'`): what a lookup reports.
  `FileMetadata.status`, `ServiceAssetMetadata.status` (`assets.service.byIds`)
  and `ApplicationFile.status` are `AssetStatus`; the file record's `status`
  admits `lost`.
- `file.lost` in `FILE_EVENT_TYPES` (`@oxy.so/core/server`): the event every
  application using the file receives, with `file.status` `lost`. Replace or
  remove what you show, as for `file.deleted`. A receiver built on an earlier
  core refuses it as not a file event.
- `fileManagement.contentLost` (en-US, es-ES).
- Pins `@oxy.so/contracts` 5.7.0.

entries.title: @oxy.so/services 12.8.0
entries.content:
Needs `@oxy.so/core` 6.11.0.

### Changed

- The follow stores and hooks hold a stable `FollowErrorCode` instead of
  English text: `useFollowTarget().error`, `useFollow().error` /
  `followData[id].error`, `useFollowForButton().error` and the `errors` maps of
  `useFollowTargetStore` and the follow store. A server refusal keeps the
  server's code and status (`offline`, `signed_out`, `forbidden`, `not_found`,
  `rate_limited`), never its message; anything else names the action
  (`read_failed`, `update_failed`, `mode_failed`).
- `FollowButton` and `FollowTargetButton` word every failure through one
  mapping onto core's `follow.errors.*` strings, in the app's language. The
  single-user `FollowButton` now shows that toast when a follow is refused,
  instead of failing silently.
- A signed-out follow from `useFollow` rejects with `OxyAuthenticationError`.

### Added

- `useFollowErrorMessage()` and the `FollowErrorCode` type, for an app that
  renders a follow hook's `error` itself.

### Removed

- The English fallbacks "Could not follow", "Could not unfollow", "Could not
  read follow status", "Failed to update follow status" and friends.

entries.title: @oxy.so/services 12.7.0
entries.content:
### Added

- `useAccountColor` (and `resolveAccountColor`) from `@oxy.so/services/ui/client`:
  one hook that applies the account's colour (`user.color`, falling back to
  `themePreference.colorPreset`) to the Bloom theme, so every Oxy app wears the
  same colour instead of each re-deriving it. The API already refuses `oxy` and
  `faircoin` to any other handle and `mono` without its benefit, on both
  fields. An app with a plan of its own passes `canUse` to withhold a name.

entries.title: @alia.onl/sdk 21.5.3
entries.content:
### Fixed

- **Every entry type-checks on its own.** `@alia.onl/sdk/text`, `/ask`, `/ask/text` and `/voice`
  reach components that use NativeWind's `className`, but only the root entry carried
  `/// <reference types="nativewind/types" />`. Expo apps load NativeWind's types themselves and
  never noticed; a consumer that does not (a Vite app) got 65 `className` errors importing
  `@alia.onl/sdk/text`. Each of those entries now carries the reference.
- `@alia.onl/sdk/avatar` no longer needs the host to declare Node's `process`: the one
  `process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_ALIA_API_URL` read declares its own type (Metro still inlines it).

### Added

- `check:entry-types` (in `prepublishOnly` and CI): compiles a consumer of each entry in
  `exports` alone, through a real `node_modules` link, with nothing loaded globally and the
  strictest consumer's options.

entries.title: @alia.onl/sdk 21.5.2
entries.content:
### Fixed

- Welcome and conversation sheets grow and shrink with their content up to Bloom’s
  available-height limit, instead of filling the entire frame. Bloom owns the Screen
  sizing, scrolling, keyboard clearance and safe areas.
- The empty thread no longer adds composer clearance a second time. Growing and
  shrinking a draft now changes the sheet height by the composer’s actual change.

### Changed

- The Bloom peer is `>=15.10.1 <16.0.0`, which provides intrinsic Screen sizing
  inside content-sized sheets and clips decorative chat backgrounds.

entries.title: @alia.onl/sdk 21.5.0
entries.content:
### Fixed

- **The SDK no longer ships every Oxy account screen to the app.** The host's app assertion
  (`useAppAssertion`) was read from `@oxy.so/services/ui`, the only entry that exported it, and
  that entry registers every account screen at import (with Bloom's phone flags and the rest), so
  every app using the SDK carried them in its first-paint JS: +0.58 MiB in CrowdSource's reviewer.
  It now comes from the lean `@oxy.so/services/ui/client`, like `useOxy` and `useAuth`.
  `check:entries` refuses `@oxy.so/services/ui` from every entry, as it already refused the root.

### Changed

- The `@oxy.so/services` peer is `>=12.1.0`, the first release whose `ui/client` exports
  `useAppAssertion`.

entries.title: @alia.onl/sdk 21.4.0
entries.content:
### Added

- **`@alia.onl/sdk/text` and `@alia.onl/sdk/ask/text`: the chat without bundling the voice
  call.** `voice={false}` hid the call, but its code still shipped: since 21.3.2 the web build
  inlines the call into the chat's chunk, so a text-only app paid for it. The new entries export
  the same `AliaChatSheet`, `AliaChatScreen` and `AliaChatContent`, and `AliaAskProvider` /
  `useAskAgent` with a lazily loaded sheet. None of them reaches the call's modules (its socket,
  protocol and audio engine), and they never offer a call. Read-aloud and dictation stay.
  CrowdSource's reviewer, which switched `AliaChatSheet` to `@alia.onl/sdk/text`: lazy sheet
  chunk 1,455,831 → 1,357,287 bytes (413.8 → 374.2 KB gzip), `__common.js` 3,978,158 →
  3,962,370 bytes, no new chunk. The README has a table of which entry to import.

### Changed

- `AliaChatContent` no longer imports the call. It draws whatever call `VoiceCallContext` hands it,
  and the root entry and `@alia.onl/sdk/ask` export their chat through `withVoiceCall`, so those
  two behave as before. `check:entries` checks that the text entries never reach the call, on any
  platform, and draw no async boundary on web other than the ask sheet's.

entries.title: @alia.onl/sdk 21.3.2
entries.content:
### Fixed

- **On web the SDK draws no async chunk boundary of its own**, so an app that lazy-loads its Alia
  sheet keeps the chat in that chunk instead of its first paint. Expo's Metro serializer hoists
  every module two async chunks share into `__common.js`, loaded at first paint; the SDK's own
  `import()` calls (the call's `VoiceSession`, the root entry's `AliaAskProvider` sheet, the
  `expo-audio`, document-picker and image readers) made such chunks inside the app's, and moved the
  whole chat and the Bloom it draws with into `__common.js`. On web those now import statically
  (`.web` forks); native keeps its lazy loads. The root entry's `AliaAskProvider` imports its sheet
  statically on every platform (the root already holds the chat); `@alia.onl/sdk/ask` keeps its
  one lazy boundary. CrowdSource's reviewer: first-paint JS 1.57 MiB gzip → 1.23 MiB, largest
  file 5.05 MiB → 3.79 MiB, its lazy Alia chunk 29 KiB → 404 KiB gzip. `check:entries` holds it.
- **The source compiles under `erasableSyntaxOnly`.** The SDK ships TypeScript source, and a
  consumer that compiles it with `erasableSyntaxOnly` (OxyHQ/website, `tsc -b`) failed with TS1294
  on two constructor parameter properties in `runtime/conversations.ts`
  (`ConversationNotFoundError.conversationId`, the offline store). They are now declared fields
  assigned in the constructor, and the SDK's own `tsconfig.json` sets `erasableSyntaxOnly`, so
  `typecheck` (CI and `prepublishOnly`) refuses parameter properties, enums and namespaces.

entries.title: @alia.onl/sdk 21.3.1
entries.content:
- Ask Alia follows the active account language resolved by Oxy Services instead of defaulting to
  English. Changes to that language update the open sheet without replacing its conversation.
- Ship a complete Spanish chat catalogue, including composer, voice, menus, thought panel and
  conversation errors. Regional Spanish tags use it; host label overrides remain supported.
- Apply the sheet's labels above its hooks and all its sheets, so sharing errors and the thought
  panel use the same language as the conversation.

entries.title: @alia.onl/sdk 21.3.0
entries.content:
The SDK runs on Expo SDK 58 (React Native 0.88, React 19.3) as well as Expo 57.

### Changed

- **Peers admit Expo SDK 58.** Every `expo-*` peer is `^57.0.0 || ^58.0.0`, `react-native` is
  `^0.86.0 || ^0.88.0` and `react-native-gesture-handler` `^2.32.0 || ^3.3.0` (SDK 58 ships 3.3).
  `@oxy.so/bloom` is `>=10.21.0`, the first Bloom whose `TextInput` ref props type-check under
  React Native 0.88's strict TypeScript API.

### Fixed

- **A picked image is read with `expo-file-system`'s `File` API** (`new File(uri).base64()`). The
  root entry's `readAsStringAsync` is the legacy API, which throws at runtime since the package
  moved it to `expo-file-system/legacy`, so attaching a photo on iOS or Android failed.
- **An edit and a regenerate call `AliaRuntimeHost.onTurnStart`**, like a send from the composer
  or a retry: each sends a new turn. A host that judges what a turn does against the moment it
  was sent (a host tool's staleness check) used to judge an edited or regenerated turn against the
  turn before it. An edit that sends nothing (an unknown message, empty content) calls nothing.

entries.title: @alia.onl/sdk 21.2.0
entries.content:
### Added

- **`parseCatalogueTool` and `toolRendererKey` from `@alia.onl/sdk/tools`.** Which app a tool call
  belongs to (`oxy_<app>__<tool>` / `self_<app>__<tool>`) is now readable without loading React
  Native, so a host's own pure models and tests — the code that decides what a screen shows —
  can tell its catalogue's results apart. The main entry exports the same two functions as before.

entries.title: @alia.onl/sdk 21.1.0
entries.content:
A shared conversation has one address, Alia's, whichever app minted it (`docs/agent-embedding.md`
§6).

### Added

- **`url` on `AliaConversationShare`**: `useShareConversation().share` (and a host's `onShare`)
  gets the link to hand on, `https://alia.onl/shared/<token>`, rather than a token to build its own
  page around.
- **`aliaSharedConversationUrl(token)`**: the same link, for an app that redirects the share links
  it minted before to Alia's page.

entries.title: @alia.onl/sdk 20.2.0
entries.content:
An app mounts its one sheet at the root without the chat in its entry bundle.

### Added

- **`@alia.onl/sdk/ask`**, a leaf entry with `AliaAskProvider` and `useAskAgent` alone. The root
  entry still exports both, but brings the whole chat with them.

### Changed

- **`AliaAskProvider` loads its sheet lazily** (`components/AliaAskSheet.tsx`, one `import()`) and
  mounts it on the first `ask`. Signed in, the module is fetched in the background, so the first
  `ask` does not wait on the network. `check:entries` holds that `./ask` loads none of the chat
  with the entry.
- **Ref and event types are React Native 0.88-ready.** A ref to a `ScrollView` or `TextInput` is
  typed `ComponentRef<typeof …>` (0.88 types both as function components), and key presses are
  `TextInputKeyPressEvent` (`TextInputKeyPressEventData` is deprecated since 0.86). Nothing
  changes on 0.86. The peer ranges stay on Expo 57 / React Native 0.86: Bloom's own `TextInput`
  ref props are not 0.88-ready yet.

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom@8.1.0
entries.content:
Bloom 8.1.0 moves agent avatars and editors to a single shared renderer, replacing the legacy WASM/SVG engines.

- Share rendering resources and load geometry and motion assets on demand while keeping each avatar's animation, gaze, reactions and computer activity independent.
- Preview shapes and eyes separately, keep color controls available, and preserve complete custom configurations independently of presets.
- Bound body pigment in the engine and match hands and fitted tufts to the avatar color.
- Improve accessory fitting and restore Felipe's authored beret placement and material.
- Update the Todd, Alfred, Iris and Felipe creation templates and versioned avatar documentation.

Validation includes 34 integration tests, 32 runtime regressions, package/export verification, consumer types, and browser checks for editors and the Website integration. The main merge additionally requires the full nine-shard CI suite.

When upgrading from 7.x, note the 8.0.0 change: import `LinkPreviewCard` and its types from `@oxy.so/bloom/link-preview`. The card supports image renditions through `expo-image`.
